Now I'll generate a summary of loss rates. Let me calculate the average loss rate and categorize items based on their distance from the average.

args.sql:
WITH loss_rate_stats AS (
  SELECT 
    AVG(loss_rate_%) AS avg_loss_rate,
    STDDEV(loss_rate_%) AS stddev_loss_rate
  FROM veg_loss_rate_df
  WHERE loss_rate_% IS NOT NULL
),
loss_rate_categories AS (
  SELECT 
    item_name,
    loss_rate_%,
    CASE 
      WHEN loss_rate_% < (avg_loss_rate - stddev_loss_rate) THEN 'Below Average'
      WHEN loss_rate_% >= (avg_loss_rate - stddev_loss_rate) AND loss_rate_% <= (avg_loss_rate + stddev_loss_rate) THEN 'Within 1 Std Dev'
      WHEN loss_rate_% > (avg_loss_rate + stddev_loss_rate) THEN 'Above Average'
    END AS category
  FROM veg_loss_rate_df, loss_rate_stats
  WHERE loss_rate_% IS NOT NULL
)
SELECT 
  avg_loss_rate,
  stddev_loss_rate,
  COUNT(*) AS total_items,
  SUM(CASE WHEN category = 'Below Average' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS below_avg_count,
  SUM(CASE WHEN category = 'Within 1 Std Dev' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS within_stddev_count,
  SUM(CASE WHEN category = 'Above Average' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS above_avg_count
FROM loss_rate_categories
GROUP BY avg_loss_rate, stddev_loss_rate;
